questions.question: Adding another resistor in SERIES always:
options: Halves the current in one branch only

questions.question: A 12 Ω and a 6 Ω resistor connected in parallel have a combined resistance of:
The built-in sanity check for any parallel calculation is that the answer must be:
options: Equal to the sum of the branches

questions.question: The 12 Ω // 6 Ω pair is wired in series with a 5 Ω resistor. The total network resistance is:
The emf of a battery is best defined as:
options: The voltage across the external resistor
The energy the battery gives each coulomb of charge, read when no current flows
The heat generated inside the battery
The current the battery can deliver

questions.question: A 9 V cell with r = 0,5 Ω drives a 4 Ω external resistor. The current in the circuit is:
In that same circuit, the terminal voltage and the lost volts are respectively:
With the switch OPEN, a voltmeter across the battery terminals reads:
options: The full emf, because no current means no lost volts

questions.question: The correct first step of the full-circuit routine is to:
options: Collapse the external network into a single equivalent resistance
Calculate the power in each resistor
Read the terminal voltage off the diagram

questions.question: An 18 V battery (r = 1 Ω) feeds a 2 Ω resistor in series with a 10 Ω // 15 Ω pair. The main current is:
In that circuit, the voltage across the 10 Ω // 15 Ω parallel pair is:
The branch currents through the 10 Ω and 15 Ω resistors are 1,2 A and 0,8 A. The junction audit confirms this because:
options: Their difference equals the lost volts
Each equals half the main current
They add up to the 2 A main current exactly

questions.question: On a terminal-voltage versus current graph for a real battery, the vertical intercept and gradient give:
options: The intercept gives the emf; the gradient gives negative r
The intercept gives r; the gradient gives the emf
The intercept gives the power; the gradient gives the current

questions.question: When an extra lamp is connected in PARALLEL across a battery, the terminal voltage:
options: Rises, because more energy is drawn
Drops, because total current rises and the lost volts I·r rise with it

questions.question: The three equivalent expressions for electrical power are:
In the 18 V circuit with a main current of 2 A and r = 1 Ω, the power wasted inside the battery is:
In the depot picture, the emf is:
options: The toll taken at the gate
The push left over on the road outside
The full push the depot promises before the toll gate

questions.question: The toll collector's merciful rule is that the lost volts are zero whenever:
An old torch cell reads full voltage on a meter but barely lights the bulb because:
options: The bulb has become more resistive
Its internal resistance has swollen, so the toll eats the push once current flows

questions.question: In the river picture, resistors in SERIES are like:
options: Obstacles one after another that every drop must pass — difficulties add

questions.question: Cutting one MORE parallel channel, even a narrow one, makes the total resistance:
options: Smaller — every new route relieves the existing ones

questions.question: The chant for what is COMMON in each layout is:
options: In series the voltage is common; in parallel the current is common
In series the current is common; in parallel the voltage is common

questions.question: Household appliances are wired in parallel so that:
options: Each draws its own current on its own branch without blocking the others
They all share one current equally
The total resistance stays as high as possible

questions.question: When the ignition key is turned, the starter motor joins the circuit as:
The four-link chain that explains the dimming headlights, in order, is:
options: External resistance falls, total current rises, lost volts rise, terminal voltage drops
Current falls, resistance rises, emf rises, lights brighten
Terminal voltage rises, current falls, toll falls, lights dim
Resistance rises, current rises, emf falls, toll disappears

questions.question: Lights dipping when a heater kicks in on the same overloaded multiplug is explained by:
options: Each new device opening a channel that raises the total current, which pays more toll along the supply
The lights sharing their current with the fridge
A drop in the mains frequency

questions.question: A battery reads a healthy voltage at rest but collapses while cranking. The mechanic's diagnosis is:
options: The starter motor is too small
Swollen internal resistance — the idle reading tested the promise, cranking tested the delivery
